Order the values of a key, and the analysis variables

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_levels.Rd

plan_levels() says the order the values of a column or analysis variable appear in — the arms across the top, the categories of SEX down the side, or the blocks of rows themselves — and may give each value its text on the way. It is a layer like every verb after table_plan(): it merges one key at a time, so a later call adds a variable without restating the rest. Values left out follow in the data's order.

Usage

plan_levels(.plan, ..., .drop_empty = NULL)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

...

One entry per column or analysis variable, named by it; the value is the order. An order may name its values' text, as base::factor()'s levels and labels do:

<key> = c("M", "F")

the order of a key's values (ARM, SEX, a value of table_plan(cols = ) or rows = ).

<key> = c(F = "Female", M = "Male")

the order F, M, and the text each prints as; an element without a name is the value as it is.

variable = c("AGE", "SEX")

the order of the analysis variables (the blocks of rows); a named element also gives the block's heading, variable = c(AGE = "Age (years)", "SEX").

A single unnamed argument that is itself a named list or vector is taken as the whole map. plan_labels() names values without ordering them, and wins value by value over a text given here.

.drop_empty

Variables whose levels no record has are not shown: a level whose n is 0 (or missing) in every column, as an ARD made with a code list's full set of levels has (a factor's unused level, counted 0). NULL (default): every level the data has is shown. A level that some column counts stays; a variable summarised without n is untouched. Several calls add up.

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb; plan_labels() for text without order.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

# Invented counts, one row a statistic: SEX has an "Unknown" level
# that no subject has.
st <- data.frame(
  ARM       = rep(c("Active", "Placebo"), each = 4),
  variable  = rep(c("AGE", "SEX", "SEX", "SEX"), 2),
  .label    = rep(c(NA, "F", "M", "U"), 2),
  .kind     = rep(c("continuous", "categorical", "categorical",
                    "categorical"), 2),
  stat_name = rep(c("mean", "n", "n", "n"), 2),
  stat      = c(63.5, 9, 11, 0, 61.2, 12, 8, 0))
p <- table_plan(st, cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(continuous = c(Mean = "{mean:.1f}"), categorical = "{n}")

# Minimal: males first
p |> plan_levels(SEX = c("M", "F", "U")) |> plan_apply("table")
#>   group label Active Placebo
#> 1   AGE  Mean   63.5    61.2
#> 2   SEX     M     11       8
#> 3   SEX     F      9      12
#> 4   SEX     U      0       0

# Placebo on the left, the SEX block first with its heading, each sex
# spelled out, and the empty "Unknown" row dropped
p |>
  plan_levels(ARM = c("Placebo", "Active"),
              variable = c(SEX = "Sex", AGE = "Age (years)"),
              SEX = c(F = "Female", M = "Male", U = "Unknown"),
              .drop_empty = "SEX") |>
  plan_apply("table")
#>         group   label Placebo Active
#> 1         Sex  Female      12      9
#> 2         Sex    Male       8     11
#> 3         Sex Unknown       0      0
#> 4 Age (years)    Mean    61.2   63.5
